title: Relaxed Bipartite Matching with Structural Inertia for Efficient Diffusion

problem.claim: Bipartite matching accelerates diffusion models through sequence reduction, but strict same-partition connectivity constraints limit semantic-connection recall and can degrade dense generative tasks.

gap.claim: Standard single-pass bipartite matching cannot merge nodes within the same partition, causing a theoretical 50% ceiling on topological recall and under-clustering.

contributions.claim: ReMatch is a training-free framework that formulates sequence reduction as a constraint-relaxation problem.
ReMatch uses cascaded independent random partitions to relax bipartite constraints and recover lost connections, while exploiting structural inertia in diffusion features to amortize update costs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show that ReMatch establishes a superior Pareto frontier.
The authors report that ReMatch addresses standard bipartite approaches' under-clustering without additional inference latency.
Code is reported as available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Bipartite matching is presented as an efficient paradigm for accelerating diffusion through sequence reduction.
The single-pass formulation imposes a strict connectivity constraint that limits semantic-connection recall to 50%.
The connectivity limitation creates partition noise and reduces fidelity on dense generative tasks.
ReMatch relaxes the matching constraint using cascaded random partitions and structural inertia in diffusion features.
The authors report a superior Pareto frontier and resolution of under-clustering without added inference latency.

source_observation.claim: Relaxing a rigid partition constraint through multiple independent partitions can recover connections excluded by a single-pass formulation.

interpretation.claim: Constraint relaxation may improve coverage when a structural restriction systematically prevents useful associations.

application.claim: For sequence-reduction systems, consider cascaded independent partitions when single-pass matching causes under-clustering.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond diffusion features or dense generative tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative evaluation values, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the exact matching algorithm, update schedule, or latency measurement protocol.
